articles.title: Jon Ossoff's decisive Senate win in Georgia fuels presidential buzz
articles.summary: Washington — Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff's commanding reelection victory in Georgia is drawing renewed attention to his potential as a 2028 presidential contender, as election data shows how he assembled a broad coalition of voters in the pivotal presidential battleground state. Despite the growing speculation, Ossoff, 39, is for now dismissing the possibility of a White House bid. During a debate in October, Ossoff said he had "zero interest in running for president" in 2028. Some early polls place him at the top of a hypothetical 2028 primary field. A post-election Emerson College survey showed Ossoff with the support of 17% of respondents — narrowly ahead of former Vice President Kamala Harris and New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, with former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and California Gov. Gavin Newsom rounding out the top five. Ossoff has attracted interest from both centrists and progressives while delivering a decisive victory in a closely divided presidential battleground state. At Crooked Con, a primarily progressive gathering in Washington after the midterms, Ossoff received 38% of first-choice votes in its straw poll, ahead of Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg. "I think he would make an attractive presidential contender on the Democratic side," said Jerry Gonzalez, CEO of GALEO Impact Fund PAC, a Georgia-based Latino political action committee that endorsed Ossoff in his Senate race. "He is not afraid, he won't shy away from holding the Trump administration accountable, but in a way that works towards actually building coalitions to get something done." Democrats who can win statewide in conservative or swing states tend to be moderate, and that's true of Ossoff, too. "He comes across, and tries to present himself, as a moderate, and he talks about issues which moderate conservatives could get behind," said Charles Bullock, a longtime political science professor at the University of Georgia. "The issues he stresses are things which are within the broad mainstream of 'These would be good things.'" It's unclear how well a moderate would fare in the early nominating states. What is effective in a Georgia general election may be a tougher sell in a Democratic primary, where voters often reward ideological purity over swing-state caution. "Obviously, he's successful here in Georgia," Bullock said. "How would he play elsewhere? "I think what we will be seeing is preparation, maybe for a later run," Bullock speculated. Ossoff's record gives rivals on both flanks openings to attack: progressives have criticized his vote for the Republican-backed Laken Riley Act and his reluctance to embrace "Medicare for All," while his votes to restrict certain weapons sales to Israel and his criticism of its military conduct in Gaza have drawn objections from some pro-Israel Democrats and donors. All of those issues are certain to be part of the 2028 primary contest. For example, Rep. Ro Khanna, another potential 2028 candidate, last week tried to restart the debate over universal healthcare. "Medicare for All means healthcare for everyone, like public school is free for every kid," Khanna wrote on X, arguing, "'Medicare for All who want it' is pablum. It's telling parents they have to pay for public school." In his reelection this month, Ossoff defeated GOP opponent Mike Collins by around 18 points, two years after President Trump defeated Harris by around two points in 2024. It was a much wider margin than his last Senate election, which he won by just over one percentage point. Powering Ossoff's win this year was a broad coalition of voters, including some swing constituencies that Democrats have struggled with in recent years, CBS News' exit polling shows. Ossoff maintained strong support among Black voters, winning 93% of the group, which make up almost one-third of the state's eligible voters according to Pew Research Center . He did not win the White voters who make up just over half of Georgia's electorate, but he did make significant inroads, winning 40% — after Harris had won just 28% two years earlier. He also notched some improvement in groups that have shifted hard against Democrats: He won 29% of White voters without college degrees (compared to Harris' 18%) and 19% of White evangelical or born-again Christian voters (compared to less than 10% for Harris). Ossoff also won men by nine points after Harris lost them by 13 points. Both Ossoff and Harris won younger Georgians, but Ossoff won them by a larger margin, securing 85% of voters ages 29 and under. Ossoff also split the 45-and-older vote roughly in half, while Harris lost that age group by a 15-point margin. And Ossoff made gains with Hispanics — a group that makes up less than 10% of Georgia's eligible voters but which has grown rapidly and has become a swing demographic that could decide a close race in the perennial battleground. In his reelection victory, he won around two-thirds of Latino voters, up seven points from Harris' performance two years earlier. A comparison of 19 Georgia precincts where at least 30% of active registered voters identify as Hispanic or Latino shows substantial Democratic improvement. Ossoff won those precincts by a combined 49 points in the two-candidate vote, compared with an eight-point advantage for Harris in the 2024 presidential election and an 18-point margin for fellow Democratic Sen. Raphael Warnock in 2022. The changes were significant in areas that had supported Mr. Trump just two years earlier. In six heavily Latino precincts in Whitfield County, the combined results shifted from a 12-point Trump advantage in 2024 to a 37-point Ossoff victory in 2026. Three similar precincts in Hall County shifted from an 11-point Trump edge to a 33-point Ossoff victory. Those figures reflect the voting behavior of entire precincts rather than individual Latino voters, and comparisons between presidential and midterm electorates are not exact. Still, they underscore how dramatically the environment changed in places with large Latino populations. Gonzalez attributed the shift in part to concerns over affordability and immigration enforcement, two issues he said weighed heavily on Latino voters in Georgia. "Things are really expensive," Gonzalez told CBS News. "The price and affordability were a big driving issue." He also pointed to the Trump administration's immigration crackdown and its impact on Latino communities in Georgia. Ossoff has investigated allegations of abuses in federal immigration detention facilities as part of his Senate oversight work. Gonzalez also credited Ossoff's success among voters across the political spectrum to his accessibility and constituent outreach. "His office is accessible to all Georgians, and that's part of the reason why he won." In this wave election, Ossoff wasn't the only Democrat to pick up ground in the midterms. Latino and Black voters, men, voters without college degrees and younger voters moved back toward Democratic candidates nationwide, a reversal after all four groups had shifted rightward in 2024. In 2028, those groups could once again play a central role in both the Democratic Party's nominating process and the general election. States with large Black and Latino populations will lead the Democratic primary calendar after the party rearranged its schedule, and Ossoff, with his strong support from both groups, would likely stand to benefit if he were to decide to run. South Carolina — where Black Democratic voters have long played an influential role in choosing the party's presidential nominee — will go first, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia. The DNC says approximately 4.2 million Latinos live across the six early nominating states, a major increase from the party's previous early-state lineup. In the general election, maintaining a strong lead with Black, Latino and younger voters — and preventing too much slippage among White and non-college-educated voters — will also be a core task for Democrats, as they seek to prevent the GOP's first non-Trump presidential candidate in over a decade from reassembling the Trump coalition. Though Ossoff says he doesn't plan a White House bid in 2028, his performance in Georgia has provided an early measure of what an electoral coalition for him could look like. "He has mentioned that he was focused on winning reelection, which he has done, so I think that gives him a little bit of latitude to think about it a little more seriously," Gonzalez said. articles.title: Iranian attacks in Strait of Hormuz hit highest levels since war began
articles.summary: A liquefied petroleum gas tanker burning in the Strait of Hormuz off the Musandam Peninsula, Oman, on Tuesday. - Lewis Pugh Foundation/AP Reported attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz are at the highest levels since the Iran war began, maritime data shows, as Tehran seeks to re-exert its control over the critical waterway amid falling oil prices. In October, the number of attacks reported to the Royal Navy-affiliated United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) exceeded 30 for the first time since the US-Iran war began in late February. As of Sunday, at least 22 attacks were reported in November, the second highest figure since the war began, according to a CNN analysis of UKMTO data. The reporting area covers the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. Before October, the number of reported attacks in the region averaged around 10 per month. Numbers vary, but data from the International Maritime Organization also points to October as having the highest number of confirmed incidents so far this year. Since the conflict began, the strait has become a heavily contested frontier , with attacks there disrupting oil and gas shipping and sparking global economic fallout. Iran began trying to halt traffic in the wake of the US-Israeli attacks that launched the war. In response, the US imposed a blockade on Iranian ports, and as CNN previously reported , Gulf producers have found ways of getting ships through the strait. Commercial traffic through the channel – through which a fifth of the world’s oil passed before the war – remains at a reduced level when compared to the 2025 baseline. As global oil prices fall and the Iran’s domestic crude revenues come under increasing strain, Tehran has been stepping up attacks, with experts saying the country is losing its leverage over the waterway and could escalate attacks further in an attempt to force concessions from Washington. No need for a deal, Trump says The International Energy Agency attributes the recent decline in oil prices to a recovery in Gulf exports. Prices also fell after the US midterm results as concerns over fresh US military action in the Middle East subsided. “Markets appear to be increasingly assuming that a return to full-scale war is unlikely and that oil supplies will gradually recover,” Hamidreza Azizi, a senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group (ICG) think tank, told CNN . “But that assumption could change quickly if Iran decides to intensify the confrontation.” A man pumps fuel at a gas station in Miami, Florida, on November 10. - Joe Raedle/Getty Images Meanwhile, Iran’s domestic oil revenues are falling sharply as the US blockade of Iranian ports continues to stifle the country’s supply of oil to global markets, according to maritime data tracking service Kpler. “Iranian oil on water outside the (US) blockade zone has hit zero as the last cargoes discharged in China earlier this month. Consequently, Iran’s oil revenues could drop to zero by mid-December,” Kpler reported in late October. US President Donald Trump said this month the US doesn’t “need a deal” with Tehran and ordered Vice President JD Vance to turn his focus elsewhere . “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed!” Trump posted on Truth Social. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” He later indicated he wouldn’t hesitate to resume military strikes in Iran if necessary. Three tankers struck in Hormuz since Friday During the latest attacks, projectiles struck three tankers exiting the strait on Friday and Saturday, according to Marisks, a maritime risk management company. Marisks did not confirm who was behind the attacks, though it said Iranian involvement was “assessed as likely.” Fire erupted aboard the Captain Leon, a Marshall Islands-flagged chemical and oil tanker, after it was struck at the bow at 3 p.m. UTC (10 a.m. ET) on Friday. All crew were reported safe, Marisks said. The Torkel, a Hong Kong-flagged crude oil tanker, caught fire after being hit in the stern at 5 a.m. UTC on Saturday (midnight ET on Saturday). Less than an hour later, the Arina, also Hong Kong-flagged, was struck in the engine room by a missile. The attacks demonstrate the “continued critical threat” to commercial shipping in the region, Marisks said, particularly through the “southern corridor” near Oman’s coastline which Iran vehemently opposes. CNN’s Eleni Giokos, Laura Sharman, Nadeen Ebrahim and Alayna Treene contributed reporting. articles.title: ICE arrests by masked agents at Seattle airport enrage passengers and state officials
articles.summary: Screams rang out on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as two masked, plainclothes federal immigration officers detained a father and daughter as they boarded a flight bound for Los Angeles. The daughter, identified by authorities as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, clung to an agent’s leg as she pleaded: “Please, I beg you, I beg you, I beg you, no.” “They’re taking my dad. ... We have a work permit,” she told fellow passengers. “I’m being arrested by ICE.” The Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrests at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport , captured on multiple videos on Saturday morning and shared on social media, enraged state and local leaders, immigrant advocates and passengers who witnessed them. ICE has increased arrests at airports over the last year, including of foreign citizens with expired U.S. visas. “ICE is completely and totally out of control,” Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson wrote on X . “Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight.” The Department of Homeland Security responded to the governor’s remarks, posting on X that officers had been targeting Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican national who overstayed his visa. During the arrest, the agency said Hernandez “hurled hot coffee on the officers.” The officers arrested Hernandez, who they said also overstayed her visa, and said she would be charged with assaulting a federal officer. In videos of the arrests, one officer appeared to have a stain on his jacket. A passenger seemingly contested that allegation, with one heard telling an officer: “She didn’t throw coffee on you, bro.” John Gaedeke, a passenger on the flight, told The Times that the plane was half loaded when he spotted the two men — who he later learned were officers — cutting the line. Gaedeke said he heard the men whisper to each other, “Should we do it? There he is, let’s go.” Soon after, Gaedeke said he saw the officers tackle a man, and “then it just turned to chaos.” People cried as they filmed, he said, and Alaska Airlines staff were “in a state of shock.” A woman standing in front of him with her young son turned her body to protect him. “She was obviously scared. Her son was petrified,” Gaedeke said, describing what unfolded as “theatrical violence.” “The instant grief from the family members, just the screaming, crying and wailing — that still sticks with me.” Gaedeke said it didn’t look to him like the coffee was thrown at the agents. In his Instagram caption, he described the incident as “the most f— up thing I have personally witnessed in this country.” The Port of Seattle, which operates the airport, said in a statement that immigration enforcement actions are conducted “without the Port’s participation or knowledge.” Port officials said they were “outraged” by what occurred and were in conversation with Homeland Security on whether protocols “were breached.” “This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred,” the statement read. Alaska Airlines said in a statement that it was “concerned” by what unfolded “during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306.” The airline said it was not provided advance notice of the enforcement action, “and we are working to understand the circumstances surrounding what occurred, including whether the proper protocols were followed.” “We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests,” they said. A GoFundMe launched for the father and daughter, which had raised more than $40,000 by Sunday morning, described the family as “very grateful for all the love and support that they have received so far from family, friends, and community leaders and members.” “Legal proceedings and the following events can be drawn out long-term and become very costly,” Yareli Farias, who described herself as a close friend of the family, wrote on GoFundMe. “The funds raised will be used for legal expenses related to this case.” In a Saturday afternoon news conference, Katie Garrow, executive secretary-treasurer of MLK Labor, which represents thousands of unionized workers at the airport, said they were alerted to the arrests by flight attendants. “They are the ones who rang the alarm that this escalation broke protocol and crossed a red line,” Garrow said. Garrow said the incident was “so disturbing and upsetting to workers” that four of the six crew members on Flight 1306 “chose not to fly” that morning. At the news conference, Ferguson called video of the arrests “horrific” and “chilling.” He described it as “the latest example of the violence that ICE has inflicted on our communities as it works to further Donald Trump’s cruel immigration agenda.” “There is no justification for this brutality,” the governor said. Ferguson said he will request that every airline in the airport call on ICE “to get out of our airports.” “We need a system of immigration enforcement and border security that is effective, ethical and humane. And ICE is not it,” he said. “It is beyond reform. ... It is time to abolish Donald Trump’s ICE.” Times staff writer Matthew Ormseth contributed to this report. articles.title: Army plans Tuesday detonation of 5 tons of explosives in Iowa as court fight continues
articles.summary: A sign sits on top of a building at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Thursday in Middletown, Iowa. - Scott Olson/Getty Images The Justice Department on Sunday asked a federal appeals court to lift its pause on a permit allowing the US Army to detonate nearly five tons of material containing lead azide at an Iowa munitions plant, saying the Army intends to carry out the detonation Tuesday. The court’s order “does not enjoin or otherwise prohibit the Army from acting under a separate legal authority,” the Justice Department argued in a filing Saturday. The Army says the degraded material could explode on its own as temperatures drop. “The real choice, in other words, is not between a detonation and no detonation. It is between a planned and mitigated detonation and an unplanned and unmitigated explosion,” the filing said. A federal appeals court temporarily paused the US Environmental Protection Agency permit that would allow the Army to detonate the material at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in tiny Middletown on Thursday after environmental groups sued. The detonation, originally scheduled for Friday morning, had been moved to Monday. The Justice Department in its filing Friday was effectively trying to bypass judicial process and review, lawyers representing the environmental groups argued. “People across numerous impacted communities speaking up and demanding accountability is the only reason there was an opportunity to pause and think about better ways to approach the lead azide problem,” Thien Chau, a senior attorney at Earthjustice, which represents the environmental groups, said in a statement Sunday. “Yet despite claiming public safety is its top priority and public communication is essential to trust, the Army seemed more concerned over the weekend with finding a way to sidestep the judicial process than on meeting the public’s demands for greater transparency, notice to affected communities, and far stronger protection of people, property, and the environment from serious harm.” The Army, in coordination with the EPA, plans to destroy nearly 70 drums of lead azide, a compound used to detonate munitions, the military branch said. Environmental groups suing the EPA said the Army as of late Sunday morning had failed to update the public about latest weather forecasts, as well as projections of the path of the plume containing lead dust. Lead is unhealthy at any level, and it’s especially dangerous to children, health officials said. The Army’s plan has drawn heavy pushback from concerned Iowans and politicians about the plume’s spread over a vast swath of Iowa, the Mississippi River and into parts of Illinois. Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds on Friday activated a state emergency operations center, while officials in nearby Illinois are warning residents about dust spilling over into their state. The Federal Aviation Administration has restricted flights around Middletown from Monday through Wednesday, according to a temporary flight restriction notice . Here’s what we know about the planned detonation and the legal fight. Army says detonation is needed The Army in March , during “ routine stockpile surveillance,” discovered lead azide housed in bunkers had been degrading, according to Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle. Officials evaluating the best way to dispose of the material communicated with “stakeholders and the public in Middletown and the modeled impact area about the danger it posed,” Telle said. The lead azide’s degraded status left it “extremely unstable and sensitive to even slight friction or movement,” according to an FAQ distributed by the Army to the community last month. “Packing and transporting it poses an unacceptable risk of accidental detonation to personnel handling and transporting as well as to the public.” After coordinating with the EPA, experts and the community, officials “determined that a controlled detonation was the option that posed the lowest risk to the public in the immediate and surrounding area,” Telle said. Army officials held an October 15 community meeting to share information about a potential detonation in late November, according to documents on the plant’s page . Then, on November 15, the community got a notice of a detonation on Friday, according to an Army news release . After pushback, the Army rescheduled the detonation to Monday – the “latest possible moment prior to a forecasted temperature drop, which would risk further destabilization of the material,” Telle said. While noting the court’s pause is still in place, the City of Fort Madison said Saturday it was notified that the detonation would most likely occur either Monday or Tuesday, but if it doesn’t happen this week, “another time will need to be arranged with additional planning.” City officials said they hadn’t been given any further information but expect the state to issue more details on Sunday. Waiting too long to detonate the lead azide could pose more hazards later, Telle said. The emergency permit from the EPA would allow the Army to do the detonation between November 13 and February 11, 2027. Still, the problem should have been evaluated 20 years ago, said Patrick O’Shaughnessy, a University of Iowa professor and environmental health expert. “Somebody left it to rot that long, for it to now being the only option is to blow it up on site because it can’t be moved,” he told CNN. “It’s regrettable, and it’s almost, it’s hard to believe that it’s happening in this country.” The Army had previously awarded a contract to MuniRem Environmental, a Georgia-based firm that uses chemicals to neutralize munitions, but later canceled the deal citing safety concerns, court filings show, as first reported by The New York Times, and instead opted to detonate the lead azide. “This decision is supported by the technical consensus across military and federal explosive safety authorities that this is the only safe method of treatment,” read a partially redacted September letter included in the court filings from Amy L. Borman, deputy assistant secretary of the Army for Environment, Safety and Occupational Health. CNN has reached out to the Army for comment. Valentine Nzengung, a chief executive at MuniRem, told CNN the Army “told us that they evaluated reports and they found out that controlled detonation was the safest way, and that is why they were moving forward with controlled detonation. They did not provide us much more detail than this.” Iowans and local officials push back Officials at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant have regularly updated officials in Middletown – home to 363 people – about the planned detonation, according to Brieanna Beck, the city clerk and municipal officer, who said she has quickly shared each update on the city’s Facebook page. The city has been aware of the detonation plan for a couple of months, she told CNN in an email. The Army plant sent letters to homes potentially affected by the detonation, Beck said. The governor’s office and state agencies were coordinating with EPA and Army officials to “continuously monitor the situation and keep local partners informed,” Reynolds said Friday. More than 80 miles north of Middletown, Cedar Rapids is preparing for the detonation. Officials in Iowa’s second-most populous city are taking steps to monitor the drinking water supply – drawn from wells along the Cedar River – for potential contamination, though they don’t anticipate impacts, according to a city update . But plans and communication around the detonation have gotten strong pushback from environmental advocates, as well as state and federal politicians in Iowa and neighboring Illinois. Officials in Iowa City, about 60 miles north of Middletown, said they didn’t know about the planned detonation until news began circulating early last week and were unaware of any state or federal agency formally notifying them, according to City Manager Geoff Fruin in a declaration on Saturday supporting the environmental groups’ lawsuit. An email Friday told the city an EPA team was deployed to collect a pre-detonation surface water sample because Iowa City, with a population of over 75,000 people, is within a 100-mile radius of the detonation, he said. Iowa City officials have been discussing possible protocols to address impacts from the detonation, Fruin said. But he added it’s difficult to plan due to “lack of notice and information.” Josh Turek, the US senator-elect for Iowa, has called for a delay to the detonation, saying he had “heard from many Iowans who are worried about their health and safety due to the potential risk of lead exposure as a result of the detonation.” Rob Sand, the incoming governor, said Iowans’ safety now and in the future should be the government’s top concern. “An unacceptable lack of communication and clarity has made Iowans understandably concerned and angry about this situation,” he said . “The public deserves to know, if this is the safest option, why other options were worse.” Parts of western and central Illinois could be affected by the lead plume under the current weather forecast, Illinois state officials said in an update Friday. Illinois health and environmental protection officials said they are monitoring the planned detonation and have issued updates to residents. Illinois agriculture officials have issued guidance to protect livestock and pets. They recommended keeping animals inside until the plume has passed and washing them to remove potential contaminants. Meanwhile, officials warned of exposure through fishing. Residents should stay indoors on the detonation day, with windows and doors closed for one to two days after as a precaution, Illinois officials said. They also encouraged people to use portable air cleaners equipped with a HEPA filter. Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker said Friday he had spoken with Telle, urging more transparency about the planned detonation. “The State is still seeking more data from them on how this could impact Illinoisans and is working to keep you informed and safe,” Pritzker said . What the court has said Environmental advocates sued the US EPA on Thursday over the emergency permit allowing the Army to detonate the lead azide, citing concerns about the potential impacts of the explosion. The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday temporarily stayed the EPA’s emergency permit until it rules on the groups’ emergency motion, but didn’t say when the court would take action on the case. The Army, in a joint statement with the US Department of Health and Human Services and the EPA, said Friday afternoon, “The entire interagency is working together to ensure that the controlled detonation in Middletown, Iowa, is conducted in the safest fashion possible.” “Officials have been meticulously planning for this event since March, and all agencies involved are prepared to take the most extreme mitigation measures available to ensure there is no risk to the public and any disruptions are minimized,” the statement said, adding they will keep local officials and the public updated. The cleanup requirements under the current permit are inadequate to properly address the scope and degree of potential impacts, according to Chau, the senior attorney at Earthjustice, who filed the lawsuit on behalf of the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club Iowa Chapter. There doesn’t appear to be sufficient understanding of how far the plume would spread, as well as which bodies of water, such as the Mississippi River, and land would be blanketed with lead dust, including where people live, Chau told reporters Friday. Environmental advocates called on state leaders, including Reynolds, to take control of communication over the planned detonation. “Iowans deserve a transparent, coordinated, and effective response to this unprecedented event,” Michael Schmidt, general counsel at the Iowa Environmental Council, said in a news briefing. The Justice Department first cited a federal regulation that exempts responses to an “immediate threat” to human health, public safety, property or the environment from EPA permitting requirements in its Friday filing. In Saturday’s filing, it said the Army intends to invoke that exemption. Col. Aaron Teller, commander of the Army’s 71st Ordnance Group, which handles explosive ordnance disposal, determined the lead azide poses “an immediate threat,” according to a sworn declaration filed with Saturday’s notice. The Justice Department has not responded to CNN’s request for comment. “We want to be absolutely clear that the regulation they cite is an extraordinary and extreme backstop for situations where there is truly nothing else that can be done,” Rachel Rintelmann, a managing attorney at Earthjustice, said in an email of the Friday filing. “It is an incredibly high bar, and we urge the Army not to rely on it if it is only doing so to sidestep the ongoing processes to obtain transparency and protections that communities, government leaders, and the law demand.” Health risks of lead exposure There is no safe level of lead in the body, Dr. Sameer Vohra, director of the Illinois Department of Public Health, said in a statement . “(And) when inhaled or swallowed, it can pose serious health risks.” With the detonation, the hope is if the lead azide spreads over a wider area, it won’t stay in high-level concentrations, according to O’Shaughnessy, the University of Iowa professor. “It’s kind of like one of these, the solution to pollution is dilution, right?” he said. There is the potential for exposure through the air during the initial plume or through touch after it has settled, he said, adding neither exposure is worse than the other because the lead will still build up in your body both ways. Lead is toxic to the brain. Exposure is known to cause serious harm to children’s health, resulting in slowed growth and development, as well as problems with learning, behavior, hearing and speech, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Environmental advocates also warn the detonation could worsen health for residents in Iowa, which has the second-highest rate of cancer of any US state and is one of only three states where the rate is rising. The local National Weather Service office forecasts cooler, drier conditions Tuesday, with highs in the upper 30s. Wind conditions could affect how far lead particles travel. Wind speeds are expected near zero Tuesday, with weak winds blowing from north to south becoming near motionless by midday, CNN meteorologist Tyler Ory said. articles.title: Rep. Virginia Foxx loses reelection bid after 11 terms in North Carolina
articles.summary: Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx has been officially unseated by Democratic challenger Chuck Hubbard in North Carolina after a recount — requested by Foxx — broke in Hubbard's favor. The Associated Press called the election for Hubbard early Sunday afternoon. Hubbard, who lost to Foxx by 19 points two years ago, said in a statement that the incumbent had "graciously conceded." "Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices," Hubbard wrote on social media. "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District." Hubbard's win marks the seventh seat Democrats flipped in the state this year despite Republican redistricting efforts last year. North Carolina will send 11 Democrats and three Republicans to Congress — a reversal of the 10-4 Republican majority voters elected in 2024. The Democratic win also notches the broader party an election-year record: Having secured 258 seats, the Democrats have won their largest share of House seats in a national election since the early '90s. Foxx had requested the recount in a letter to election officials on Nov. 17, when the margin between the two candidates was 331 votes. In her letter to the State Board of Election, Foxx cited a state law that allows candidates to request a recount when the margin of victory is less than 1 percent. Foxx was first elected in 2004. Now 83, she is finishing her 11th term and has already filed paperwork to run in the 2028 race. articles.title: Israeli settlers launch attacks in West Bank as Netanyahu rival decries 'Jewish terrorism'
articles.summary: Israeli settlers launched a series of attacks across the occupied West Bank, torching at least a dozen cars and vandalizing several homes overnight Sunday, in what Gadi Eisenkot , the main rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, decried as “Jewish terrorism.” Video from the village of Kufr Malik, about 10 miles northeast of Ramallah, the seat of the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank, showed several cars in flames with thick smoke pouring into the sky as a siren blares in the background. In the same village, a home was tagged with Hebrew graffiti, including the word “revenge.” Similar scenes unfolded in the nearby villages of Deir as-Sudan and Deir Abu Masha’al, two Palestinian communities northwest of Ramallah that were also attacked by settlers. Mustafa Barghouti, the president of the Palestinian National Initiative, said the brazen attacks were part of an escalating pattern of settler violence. unknown content item - “Palestinian families are facing violence, destruction and the loss of their homes,” he said on X. Eisenkot said the violence was the result of the policies of pro-settler, far-right politicians Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who he said “brought the area to the brink of anarchy.” Smotrich was the key architect of a massive expansion of Israeli settlements and outposts in the West Bank over the last four years, while Ben-Gvir has been accused of turning a blind eye to settler violence. Eisenkot said the attacks were “acts of Jewish terrorism, and we must call them by their name.” Eisenkot, who has four more weeks to attempt to form a government and oust Netanyahu, said the Israeli government should use administrative detention and targeted operations against the assailants. A Palestinian man inspects a damaged car, which Palestinians say were burned by Israeli settlers, in Kafr Malik, near Ramallah. - Mohamad Torokman/Reuters Netanyahu has not issued any public statement about the attacks. CNN has reached out to his office for comment. Netanyahu has repeatedly tried to downplay settler violence, previously saying it was the result of what he has called “juvenile delinquents.” The West Bank has seen a surge in settler violence in recent months, particularly around the annual olive harvest, where Palestinians have repeatedly been harassed and attacked. There have been 410 settler attacks related to the olive harvest since the beginning of September, according to the UN. This weekend’s attacks occurred across several locations in the middle of the night. There were no reports of injuries. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it also received reports of an attack on the Palestinian village of At-Turwani in the southern West Bank near the city of Hebron. The IDF said in a statement it “condemns acts of violence of this nature, which harm public order.” Israeli police said on Sunday they would enter the Palestinian villages under IDF escort to collect evidence. Police have not announced any arrests after the attacks. “Settler terrorism in the West Bank does not take place in a vacuum,” said Yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Arab Joint List party, which saw a surge in support in recent elections. “It is the direct result of the deepening occupation and a government policy under which violence against Palestinians has become an everyday occurrence.” The attacks on Palestinian villages and sites have not been limited to the West Bank. On Thursday morning, a mosque in northern Israel was torched and vandalized with graffiti similar to the messages sprayed across Palestinian homes in the West Bank. Pictures shared by Arab lawmaker Ahmad Tibi showed the inside of the mosque burned and charred. He blamed anti-Arab rhetoric and “people who were poisoned by Netanyahu’s incitement” for the arson. “The police and the Shin Bet must get to the perpetrators. And immediately,” he said on X. Zeena Saifi contributed reporting. articles.title: Democrats clinch a historic House majority of at least 258 seats — the largest since 1992
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — House Democrats have secured their best general election result in decades, winning at least 258 seats in an election sweep unseen since 1992 that creates not only vast opportunities to govern but also intense pressure to deliver on campaign promises and priorities. Democrats have gained 44 House seats so far, four more than the 40 they picked up in President Donald Trump’s first midterm in 2018. The 258-seat tally was reached Sunday after Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. Four other House races remain outstanding: one each in Minnesota and Tennessee and two in Louisiana that are heading to a December runoff. Republicans will have at least 173 seats in the minority. The milestone in the 435-member House sets up divided government, with the Senate also in Democratic hands and with a Republican president in the White House. Emboldened Democrats are preparing a 100-day agenda to address high costs of living while also confronting Trump with a vast oversight agenda for the remainder of his second term in office. The Democrats’ majority will be bigger than any the party has seen in elections since Bill Clinton was first elected president in 1992 (258) or the election of Barack Obama in 2008 (257), yet not quite the high-water mark of the Franklin D. Roosevelt-era, which saw House Democratic majorities swell past 300. It presents opportunities and challenges ahead. “Like, hell yeah, we should feel pressure,” said Democratic Rep. Jason Crow of Colorado, a former Army Ranger. “There are people dying in this country and people losing their healthcare, losing their livelihoods, losing their farms, being terrorized from ICE," he said earlier this month at the Capitol, referring to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. "If you don't feel a sense of urgency and pressure in this job, and a desperation to deliver for folks, then you don't belong under this Capitol dome." Election rout creates a mandate to govern The numbers underscore the extraordinary scale of Democratic wins , which spanned from the strongest Republican states to the Midwest and East Coast , as voters, angry over high prices and the Iran war and concerned over corruption, made clear their discontent with Trump. Taking control of both the House and the Senate come January, the Democrats will carry with them the backing of voters and the expectations to deliver. The Senate Democrats won a 56-seat majority in the 100-member chamber, their biggest advantage in over a decade. The Democrats, as part of their 100-day agenda, are planning swift votes to reverse the Republicans’ Medicaid cuts and restore the Affordable Care Act tax credits the Republicans allowed to expire. Democrats have vowed to marshal their subpoena powers and launch a flurry of investigations to exert the role of Congress as a check on presidential power. That includes plans to probe how Trump and his family have become wealthier since he returned to office. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, who is in line to become House speaker, has not ruled out trying to impeach Trump for a third time. “This is a historic moment for our country. This is one of the largest classes we have seen,” said progressive leader Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., at the Capitol. She called the big numbers "a mandate for change.” Rep. Tom Suozzi, a centrist Democrat from New York and an accountant by profession, said the House Democrats should focus 75% of their time on affordability issues and 25% on accountability. “Everything should be tied back to the people — and how it’s affecting the people,” he said. For example, he said, as the Democrats launch investigations into Trump's financial dealings, they should be connecting the dots: “How does that affect people’s pocketbooks?” The White House has issued a warning to Democrats over their planned probes into the administration , going as far as claiming that such investigations — a standard oversight function of Congress — may amount to “blatant criminality.” A new generation of leaders After House Speaker Mike Johnson , R-La., struggled to keep the House functioning for the past two years with a narrow single-digit majority — meaning a few GOP lawmakers could derail the agenda — the Democrats will have a wide margin that provides the new leadership much more room to maneuver. Jeffries, who is poised to make history as the first Black speaker of the House if his colleagues elect him to the job on Jan. 3, 2027, will be able to lose dozens of Democrats on any given vote and still have the 218 needed for passage, in the face of GOP opposition. "We're not a monolith — people come to the caucus with different ideas — it's OK,” said Rep. Troy Carter, D-La., who is expected to lead the Congressional Black Caucus. Republicans saw their number of House seats fall to one of the lowest tallies in decades. They're far from the end of the Obama administration, when the House Republicans won 247 seats in the 2014 election and the rise of Newt Gingrich when they won 230 seats in 1994. Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, who was elected by his colleagues to be the Republican leader in the minority, vowed to fight their way back to power. “Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families,” Jordan said. The GOP's high-water marks include the 1920 election, with 301 seats for House Republicans. ___ Follow the AP's coverage of the 2026 elections at https://apnews.com/hub/elections This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/democrats-clinch-historic-house-majority-180701917.html

articles.title: World's longest climate summit ends without a deal after fossil fuel dispute
articles.summary: The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey descended into disarray and disappointment after countries were unable to reach consensus on a deal that failed to mention fossil fuels. Nations rejected the agreement at a fraught closing session in Antalya on Sunday, almost two days after the summit was due to finish in what stretched to become the longest Cop in history. The European Union , the UK and small island states such as Tuvalu refused to accept the text over the absence of references to fossil fuels, blasting the omissions as “greenwashing” and accusing oil states of “hijacking” the talks. Ireland’s minister for climate Darragh O’Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU, called the text “unconscionable” and said its ambition went “nowhere near the level of action that's required to deal with climate change”. A spokesperson for the British delegation said it was “profoundly disappointed” by the proposed deal. Some nations indicated a willingness to continue working, but at the closing plenary summit president ⁠Murat ​Kurum said ⁠there would be no new ⁠draft of the ​deal. COP31 president Murat Kurum leaves after the final plenary session on the second overtime day on Sunday (Getty) Andy Burnham was the only G7 leader to attend the summit, where he made an impassioned speech promising to usher in a “new era of British leadership" on climate change. But the prime minister said nothing on Sunday as hopes of a deal evaporated and delegates eventually left empty handed. UK energy secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh later called the failure to reach a deal “immensely disappointing”, but said there had been “genuine progress” during the conference. “This Cop sought to confront hard truths – that global warming is set to overshoot 1.5C and that we must act with ever more urgency to address it,” she said in a statement. “The moment required bold ambition and we have been working tirelessly to try to build consensus. It is immensely disappointing we have been unable to do so.” The failed deal had acknowledged the planet's projected temperature overshoot for the first time and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse it. It was already heavily criticised by small islands and civil society groups who called it a “betrayal” and criticised its reliance on carbon capture schemes, which had been pushed by oil states including Saudi Arabia. "It seems like we are negotiating with the Saudis," Maina Talia, Tuvalu's climate minister, commented during the conference. A representative for the Saudi delegation, which supported the deal's mention of carbon removal, told the summit he was surprised at the ‌resistance to technology, which he said offered a “concrete solution”. Ireland's minister for climate, environment, energy and transport Darragh O'Brien (L) had criticised the draft deal (AFP/Getty) Developing countries had also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient new funds to ​help them adapt to a warming planet. China and India said they had objections but chose to accept the cover text to move things forward. The Cop process is the main vehicle through which countries coordinate efforts to curb global warming. Its annual meeting provides an opportunity for nations to signal they are willing to work together to find solutions and help finance the problems rising temperatures cause. Earlier, Mr Kurum, defended the text and said the presidencies had “listened to everyone” and tried to bring the groups together, but admitted there was “no consensus”. Despite a failure to strike a deal, Mr Kurum said the summit had come to smaller agreements on plans to scale up global geothermal energy supply by 2050, build greener freight corridors and increase the electricity share of global energy to 35% by 2035. Australia's Cop31 president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, called the outcome "very disappointing" and said disagreements over fuels ​and ⁠climate finance were the dealbreakers. The conference became the longest COP ever on Sunday afternoon, passing COP25 in Madrid in 2019, which ran 44 hours over its schedule. Delegates pored over several drafts with language that tried to bridge the position of countries most exposed to climate impacts and those whose economies depend on producing or consuming fossil fuels, but the split came down to whether the text should refer to oil, gas and coal at all. The first time the transition away from fossil fuels found a mention in a UN climate agreement was at Cop28 in Dubai in 2023. It had been hoped that a series of climate disasters in the lead up to this year’s conference would help to sharpen minds and reaffirm commitments. The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all was in Copenhagen in 2009. Chief executive of environmental charity Friends of the Earth Asad Rehman said the deal in its current form “is no deal at all” and urged governments to pledge more than “wooly” promises. He warned leaders the “clock is ticking” and said governments must “come back to the negotiating table ready to deliver”. United Nations secretary-general Antonio Guterres also said he was "deeply disappointed” by the conference’s failure to reach a consensus. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” he said. "There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science." Some campaigners also turned on the EU, which rejected the text while some lauded the resistance shown at the plenary. "The EU is trying to shift blame onto others and it is deeply hypocritical. At the beginning of COP31, it signalled it was prepared to drop the renewables ask from the electrification target and it has failed to put forward an EU fossil fuel transition roadmap," said Laurie van der Burg of Oil Change International. The failure is a blow to efforts to ratchet up international ‌action, but does not erase the obligations agreed by previous ‌summits or remove existing agreements on action against climate change. articles.title: NYC releases 84,000 more 9/11 records as portal tops 11 million visits
articles.summary: The Tribute in Light is illuminated on the skyline of lower Manhattan in New York City on Sept. 11, 2024. (LEONARDO MUNOZ/Getty Images) New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's administration released 84,000 more records Sunday on the city's response to the Sept. 11 attacks, pushing its public portal past 440,000 pages as unique visits topped 11 million. The batch is the third installment under a settlement with 9/11 Health Watch, an advocacy group created by the New York State AFL-CIO, and City Hall said more records will follow in the coming months. Mamdani's fiscal 2027 budget sets aside $34 million to build and maintain the portal. "More than 11 million visits and 440,000 pages later, our work is not finished," Mamdani said in a statement . Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal framed each release as a step toward answering when City Hall learned the air at ground zero could make people sick. The city counts its releases in records but measures the archive in pages. An October installment of 40,000 records lifted the total to more than 200,000 pages, up from roughly 170,000 at the portal's September launch . That first release included the so-called Harding Memo, an undated letter to Robert Harding, a deputy mayor under former Mayor Rudy Giuliani, that listed potential grounds for lawsuits against the city, including health advisories that sent people back into the area too soon. It also included the "68 boxes" of Department of Environmental Protection files that the city said went unlocated until 2025 despite repeated requests under the state's public records law. The releases have drawn pushback from Giuliani's camp. His spokesman, Ted Goodman, accused Mamdani in September of trying to score political points by blaming local officials rather than radical Islam, and Giuliani said the terrorists bore full responsibility while faulting the Environmental Protection Agency for declaring air samples safe, NBC New York reported . The disclosures followed a courtroom loss for the city. In a May 28 decision, Justice James G. Clynes of the New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan, the state's trial-level court, found the department had acted "arbitrarily and capriciously," meaning without a reasonable basis, in denying the group's records request, according to the settlement signed Sept. 2. The deal requires monthly meetings for a year to review how many documents and pages the city has posted, plus a log of records it located but withheld. Separately, the city's Department of Investigation, its internal watchdog agency, is examining what officials knew about post-9/11 air quality and when they knew it, in an inquiry mandated by the City Council, amNY reported . © 2026 Newsmax. articles.title: Trump's intelligence chief says Putin is 'not America's friend in Ukraine'
articles.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said Sunday that President Donald Trump's use of the term "friend" to describe his relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin was "entirely appropriate" in the context of last week's summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, but said Putin "is not America's friend in Ukraine." "That conversation, that picture -- historic, historic picture -- was in the context of the three nuclear powers, the three main nuclear powers, getting together and saying, 'We cannot have a nuclear incident,'" Clayton told ABC "This Week" co-anchor Jonathan Karl. "In that circle of that conversation, using the term 'friend' is entirely appropriate." ABC News - PHOTO: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton appears on ABC News' "This Week." After Trump greeted Putin as his "friend" at the summit in China, he declined to say whether the Russian president is a friend to the U.S. at a White House press briefing Friday, saying he "can't speak to America." On Saturday, the president posted a photo on his social media platform of himself and Putin with the text "My Friend" bolded above the photo. "Is Vladimir Putin America's friend? Because Trump said he couldn't answer that question," Karl pressed Clayton. "Is Vladimir Putin America's friend? He is not America's friend in Ukraine. Not at all. Not at all," Clayton responded. Win McNamee/Pool via AP - PHOTO: Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting, November 19, 2026 in Shenzhen, China. Jan. 6 attack Michael LoSapio, Trump's nominee to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency, made headlines earlier this this week at a congressional hearing with his refusal to say whether the Capitol was attacked on Jan. 6, 2021. Karl asked Clayton the same question. Clayton also refused to directly answer, telling Karl, "I'm not going to relitigate that issue here." Pressed to respond, Clayton said, "The American people saw what happened that day. It was a very unfortunate day for America." "Does everybody who saw that wish it never happened? Absolutely, but I'm not going to get into the political characterizations in the hearings like that," Clayton continued. "We all condemn violence," Clayton said when pressed further, adding, "There is no place for violence in America." "There was violence. You can call it what you want. Every American can call it what you want. There was clearly violence," Clayton said. Recent tech outages After a slew of high-profile tech outages, sources told that the FBI and the U.S. Department of Agriculture were hit with cyberattacks late last week. Clayton told "This Week" on Sunday that he could not "get into the specifics" of those incidents. "We have highly professional people at the FBI who handle both private sector and public sector incidents like this, and I'm sure we'll get the answers in due course, just as we've gotten the answers to the incidents that happened this past week at the NSA, at Microsoft, at other places," Clayton said. As the Trump administration has explained, many of the outages in recent weeks have come during repairs to infrastructure patches identified by artificial intelligence. White House replaces national cyber director amid widespread tech outages "We have a step change in technology that we're facing with super intelligence and computing power that is expanding exponentially. And we have a dated digital infrastructure. The need to improve our digital infrastructure is clear, and that is the dynamic that we have today," Clayton said. Clayton maintained that the recent outages were not coordinated or state-sponsored. "The incidents that we saw during the course of this week, we know that they were not coordinated and that they were not state-sponsored," Clayton said. "Companies and the government, we should all be transparent with the American people that we have dated systems in a highly-evolving environment where they need to be upgraded in order to have cybersecurity," he added. Clayton said there has been an increase in cyberattacks, "but this is something that we have had for a long time." articles.title: 当前红利资产估值还有多少空间?
articles.summary: 下半年以来，以红利为主的稳定价值类资产的超额收益持续扩大，股息率与潜在回报率水平也进一步被压缩。 当前红利资产到底贵不贵，估值还有多少上行空间？ 我们从价值类资产的筛选逻辑、估值定价、预期收益率等角度讨论以下七个问题： 第一，如何构建稳定价值资产包。 我们从行业和个股两个层面筛选ROE高且稳定的资产：行业层面以ROE中位数和变异系数筛出稳定价值类三级行业，个股层面在这些行业中构建行业优先资产包，同时在全市场按相同条件构建全市场资产包。按超额收益对利率、股债差和市场涨跌的敏感度，资产可进一步分为逆周期与顺周期两类，前者在市场调整和利率下行阶段相对占优，后者在需求回升和利率上行阶段表现更好。 第二，稳定价值类资产如何估值。 盈利持续、稳定的资产适合用现金流贴现模型定价。在剩余股利政策的假设下，理论PB由ROE、分红率、增长率和贴现率共同决定，可按一阶段、二阶段和三阶段增长分别测算。 第三，贴现率如何确定。一是参考市场交易结果，当前A股电信、公用事业等稳定类行业隐含的贴现率在7%左右，日本公用事业、电信等行业估值对应的贴现率多在5%至6%，美国多在8%至9%；二是采用无风险利率加风险溢价的理论公式，2023年以来的要求回报率大致在6.5%至7.5%。 第四，盈利波动上升时需要多少股息率补偿。 以水电为基准，按盈利波动调整风险溢价，可以得到与盈利波动相匹配的应有股息率，ROE标准差每上升1个百分点，应有股息率约提高0.9个百分点。行业层面，高速公路等低波动行业的应有股息率略高于水电，动力煤等高波动行业则明显更高。具体来看，应有的理论股息率的测算结果可以概括为两条经验关系： 以变异系数测量：应有股息率≈2.2+9.1×ROE变异系数 以标准差测量：应有股息率≈2.1+0.9×ROE标准差（百分点） 第五，当前价值资产的估值低洼在哪。 用分阶段DCF模型测算稳定价值个股的理论估值，家电、医药、汽车、建材与路桥、部分城商行和股份行以及部分资源股的PB低于理论值，水电和国有大行的估值已接近或高于理论值。 第六，价值资产抬估值的空间有多少。 利率下行是2023年以来价值资产估值抬升的重要原因，但利率越低，同样幅度的下行带来的估值抬升越小。若无风险利率由1.5%降至1.0%，ROE在10%至20%的资产理论估值约有15%左右的抬升空间。 第七，如何构建估值走廊。 对盈利稳定、透明的资产，以当期盈利和贴现率测算理论PB，取其0.8至1.2倍作为估值走廊。中证红利、水电、国有大行、高速公路等的估值多在走廊内波动，估值有中枢回归的特征。目前典型红利资产距离估值上沿（1.2倍理论PB）的估值溢价空间大概还有6~12%。 本文来源： 广发策略 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 为马斯克融资买GPU，高盛“秀操作”
articles.summary: 周四，高盛联手阿波罗全球管理公司（Apollo Global Management），协助马斯克旗下的SpaceX完成了约320亿美元债券定价。这批兼具公司债与资产支持证券（ABS）特征的债券，是高盛耗时一年多交出的答卷——试图在不压垮企业资产负债表的前提下，为昂贵的AI芯片找到买单方案。 这笔债券属于SpaceX总额约440亿美元整体融资的核心部分，虽获贝莱德、Pimco等机构认购，但SpaceX为此支付了高昂成本。 本周，市场对AI增长前景的担忧拖累全球市场，美股下跌8.6%。随着支撑全球经济的AI基建不断逼近融资市场极限，这笔高成本交易正被视作其他科技巨头日后采购芯片的潜在范本。 万亿芯片融资的“两难” 给AI芯片融资历来棘手。芯片价格昂贵，使用寿命却只有短短数年。许多采购方不愿发行常规公司债，担心整体债务膨胀、拖累信用评级。 借助ABS等复杂工具举债，虽能避免新增债务冲击信用评级，却会带来新问题：ABS市场可能不够大。据Diameter的Goodwin估算，未来市场需采购约1.5万亿美元芯片，其中大部分将依赖债务融资。放眼信贷市场，唯有存量约8.3万亿美元的美国投资级公司债市场具备相近的承接体量。 摩根大通分析师今年6月在报告中写道：“找到合适的芯片融资范式是一个价值十亿美元的问题”，“在某个阶段，需要创造力来匹配AI芯片领域庞大的资金需求，以及五年期久期上相对有限的资本供给”。 跨界结构与“倒置”流程 据知情人士透露，高盛今年夏天向SpaceX抛出了破题方案：由一家特殊目的载体（SPV）采购英伟达芯片并发行债券，再通过与这家火箭、卫星及AI公司签订的约五年期租约还本付息。这套架构本质上是ABS，但债券保留了常规公司债的部分特征，包括配有美国证券统一识别码（CUSIP），从而吸引到专注高等级公司债的投资者。 相比此前支持Anthropic算力扩张的350亿美元融资项目“Big Sky”，高盛还把资金流程“倒了过来”。Big Sky通过私募配售让投资者承诺出资，等设备到位后再分批提款，债券随后才转为可供更广泛机构交易的格式。这种分阶段做法增加了复杂度，初期也限制了交易，对习惯随时买卖的公司债买家并不友好。 高盛给SpaceX的方案要求投资者预先全额出资。芯片交付前，资金先存入专用账户，可配置美国短期国债等短期工具，以产生的收益对冲设备就位前的融资成本。待GPU陆续交付，账户再放款采购并出租给SpaceX。债券一经发行，合格机构投资者即可直接交易，不必等待分批提款。 机构买单，但溢价高昂 SpaceX这笔整体融资总规模约440亿美元，包含优先和次级部分。据知情人士透露，整体买方覆盖保险公司、结构化信贷买家、资产管理机构及养老基金。在周四定价的约320亿美元债券中，约60亿美元于本周完成了银团分销。 SpaceX披露，交易支持方包括贝莱德、KKR和高盛资产管理。知情人士称，太平洋投资管理公司（Pimco）认购了约40亿美元，Blue Owl也是基石投资者之一。 不过，为了吸引买盘，SpaceX付出了高额溢价。本周向公司债买家发售的证券，定价较SpaceX今年早些时候发行的同期限债券高出约100个基点；而这批旧债近期在二级市场的跌幅持续扩大，已令债券交易员感到震惊。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 当地时间11月21日，特斯拉正式启动FSD（Full Self-Driving，完全自动驾驶）V15监督版推送。特斯拉称，新版本将升级端到端自动驾驶网络的多个环节，重点改善安全关键场景处理能力，并推出全新的驾驶可视化界面Tesla Reality View。 特斯拉CEO马斯克随后表示，FSD V15将于12月向更多用户广泛推送，称这一版本将带来“特别的东西”（Something special），并对新版本的可视化界面给予积极评价。 从此次公布的更新内容来看，FSD V15的升级不仅涉及驾驶算法，也涵盖道路环境感知、导航决策和驾驶交互等多个方面。 在安全能力方面，特斯拉方面称，V15通过升级视觉编码器，使安全关键场景的处理能力提升25倍。该视觉编码器将由FSD、Robotaxi（自动驾驶出租车）和Optimus人形机器人共享，并通过数百万条互联网视频进行训练，以提高模型的泛化能力和数据利用效率。 在具体驾驶场景中，V15重点改善了道路标志、小型动物、道路杂物及链条等物体的识别能力，同时提升了对坑洼路面和道路细节的检测能力，并增强对较深积水区域的规避能力。此外，新版本还优化了学校区域及恶劣天气下的速度控制表现，并增加识别测速摄像头后主动减速的功能。 值得关注的是，特斯拉此次推出了名为Tesla Reality View的（实景视图）新功能。根据软件更新说明，该功能将原有多个模型信号整合为端到端驾驶可视化画面(车机屏幕上可显示摄像头画面叠加FSD行驶规划)，实时呈现车辆周围的道路环境，并让驾驶员了解FSD系统正在规划的驾驶动作。用户可以在全屏可视化、地图及分屏模式之间切换。 这一功能也冲上微博热搜，引发讨论。 在导航方面，V15开始利用车队积累的路线偏好数据，通过端到端学习优化行程起点和终点的导航选择，后续版本还计划将这一能力扩展至完整行驶路线。同时，新版本还将结合用户以往的停车习惯，优化目的地停车位置的选择，并在地图上显示多个停车选项。 此外，V15还优化了驾驶员监控功能，扩大佩戴帽子、太阳镜等情况下视觉注意力监测的适用范围，并调整部分高速驾驶场景下的监控策略。新版本还增加了自行车架模式，符合条件的车辆在安装自行车架等相关拖挂配件时，也可以使用FSD。 对于特斯拉而言，V15的推出不仅关系到消费者使用体验，也与Robotaxi业务的规模化进程密切相关。FSD与Robotaxi共享视觉编码器等技术架构，意味着乘用车端积累的数据和模型能力有望与自动驾驶出行服务形成协同。 从用户采用情况来看，FSD正在成为特斯拉新车销售的重要附加服务。特斯拉2026年第三季度财报显示，当季北美新车交付中，附加FSD订阅的比例超过75%，较上一季度提高近20个百分点。与此同时，截至三季度末，特斯拉披露的全球活跃FSD订阅数（包含一次性付费购买和月度订阅用户）量达到174万，同比增长67%。 从市场落地情况来看，特斯拉FSD正在加快全球市场扩张。根据特斯拉官方最新公布的信息，FSD（Supervised）目前已在美国、加拿大、中国（China）、墨西哥、波多黎各、澳大利亚、新西兰、韩国、荷兰、立陶宛、爱沙尼亚、丹麦、比利时、斯洛文尼亚、捷克、克罗地亚、斯洛伐克、拉脱维亚、芬兰和意大利等20个国家和地区开放。 中国市场方面，11月22日，《每日经济新闻》记者向特斯拉中国方面了解辅助驾驶落地情况，官方客服表示：“我们正根据国家近年的相关法规要求，积极推进特斯拉辅助驾驶软件的相关准备工作。” 值得注意的是，同日，一名特斯拉中国销售人员向记者分享了FSD V15推送情况。记者随后在该销售人员与消费者沟通的社交平台上发现，其还展示了特斯拉FSD从2020年至2026年的用户界面（UI）变化，并以“买车就买升级上限最高的”强调特斯拉车辆后续的软件升级能力。 尽管FSD的全球落地范围不断扩大，但不同国家和地区的监管要求、车辆硬件配置及功能开放程度仍存在差异。特斯拉方面同时强调，FSD（Supervised）仍属于需要驾驶员监督的辅助驾驶系统，驾驶员必须始终保持对道路环境的关注。 本文来源： 每日经济新闻 (ID:gh_2424e6d48203) 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 黄仁勋事件后美对华算力管制走向何方？
articles.summary: 2026年11月12日，执掌英伟达三十三年的联合创始人黄仁勋辞去总裁、首席执行官及董事职务，由首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）出任临时首席执行官，资深董事哈维·琼斯（Harvey C. Jones）出任公司历史上首位董事会主席。引发此次人事变动的直接导火索，是《纽约时报》自10月下旬起连续披露黄仁勋与新加坡算力云服务商 Megaspeed 前高管的私人往来及美国情报机构的反情报调查，叠加公司内部高管关系争议，消息发酵两周内英伟达市值回落逾 6000 亿美元。 如果仅从公司治理角度观察，这是一次规避合规风险的高管切割；但放在全球半导体产业与大国科技博弈的框架下，黄仁勋的离任可谓移除了过去四年横亘在美国国家安全强硬派与跨境商业算力供给之间的最关键协调支点。自 2022 年美国升级半导体出口管制以来，中美算力领域之所以仍保留一定程度的商业缓冲，很大程度上源于黄仁勋主导的双重安排。在产业端，他利用英伟达充沛的现金流与高达 5300 亿美元的表外担保承诺，为全球新兴算力云服务商提供信用背书，维持了庞大的第三方算力租赁市场；在政策端，他长期向华盛顿决策层强调维持中国人工智能开发者对美系软件生态依赖的商业价值，为减配版芯片对华销售及海外机房远程算力租赁争取了现实空间。随着黄仁勋在国安问责压力下离职，加上民主党在 2026 年 11 月中期选举中重夺国会参众两院控制权，美国对华算力管制正由行政部门保留谈判弹性的规章管理，转向国会主导的成文法约束。 就在黄仁勋离职四天后的 11 月 16 日，美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）便发布《应对先进半导体远程访问》暂行最终规则，率先将中国企业境外租用先进算力及新马等五国芯片准入纳入许可审查。下一阶段管控将围绕云端远程访问许可、芯片内置位置核验、盟友设备出口对齐以及国会前置审批四个方向同步收紧。 外部监管机制的硬化将深刻改变中国人工智能产业的资源配置方式。短期内，东南亚与中东等离岸算力租赁渠道的合规清退，将抬高国内前沿大模型团队获取大规模训练集群的成本，促使研发重心进一步向稀疏架构与单次词元生成效率集中。从中长期看，外部算力获取通道的收窄消除了国内头部机构继续观望美系硬件供给的预期，推动核心算法工程力量转入国产算力体系完成软硬件联合迭代。与此同时，过去中美工程师围绕通用图形处理器共同优化全球开源推理框架的协作关系也将随之弱化，全球算力基础设施逐步演变为两套有所联系但独立演进技术体系的前景日渐清晰。 第一章  英伟达权力交接背后的政商结构变化 1.1 反情报审查触发英伟达管理层更迭 在市值超过四万亿美元的大型科技企业中，英伟达长期保持着鲜明的创始人主导特征，产品路线定夺、核心供应链锁单与政府关系斡旋均高度集中于黄仁勋个人。2026 年 11 月 8 日，英伟达董事会就媒体曝光的高管私人关系问题宣布启动独立调查时，声明措辞仍强调对黄仁勋及其管理团队抱有信心；然而仅隔三天，董事会便于 11 月 11 日正式接受其辞呈并立即生效。促使董事会在极短时间内改变态度的核心因素，并非单纯的企业内部伦理争议，而是个人丑闻与跨境算力流向调查交织后引发的国家安全问责风险。 此次争议的核心关联方新加坡数据中心运营商 Megaspeed International，于 2023 年从中国游戏企业剥离重组并成为英伟达官方云合作伙伴，在 2023 年至 2025 年间累计采购了至少 46 亿美元的英伟达硬件，在东南亚建设算力集群并向包括中国大型科技企业在内的客户出租算力。尽管中方明确驳斥了有关涉事人员具情报背景的说法，涉事企业也否认存在违规物理转运芯片的行为，但有研究机构基于全球加速器出货与电力消耗模型的估算显示，近年仍有相当算力规模的受限英伟达芯片经由不同渠道进入中国市场。在美国司法部、联邦调查局与国会相关委员会同时介入核查的背景下，若创始人继续留任，英伟达不仅面临漫长的国会听证消耗，其面向全球市场的出口许可审批也可能遭遇行政冻结。由长期负责财务合规的克雷斯出任临时首席执行官并增设独立董事长职位，本质上是董事会为隔离政治与监管冲击所采取的防御性制度安排。 1.2 创始人信用退潮收紧全球算力融资链条 黄仁勋离任对全球算力供给结构的直接影响，首先体现在英伟达作为行业信用中介功能的减弱。在内部管理上，英伟达过去约有 60 名高管直接向黄仁勋汇报，公司既未设置常规意义上的二号行政主管，也较少受短期财务比率束缚。依托这一决策机制，黄仁勋将英伟达庞大的自由现金流与资产负债表转化成下游算力基础设施扩张的融资杠杆。根据英伟达 2027 财年第二季度财报披露的数据，公司表外担保总额已由上一季度的 1840 亿美元大幅增加至 5300 亿美元，其中包含为新兴算力云服务商提供的 360 亿美元“照付不议”容量兜底协议，此外还持有约 990 亿美元的产业链股权投资组合。 从金融机制看，这套表外承诺相当于英伟达用自身信用为下游客户增信。大量本身缺乏投资级评级的新兴算力云服务商与初创实验室，凭借英伟达出具的最低租金保底或机房租约担保，得以按较低利率从债权市场筹集资金，再回流采购英伟达的高毛利硬件。在上游制造端，英伟达单季度的供应链与产能采购承诺额也从 1190 亿美元上升至 2790 亿美元，主要投向高带宽内存与先进封装产能；借助黄仁勋与韩国存储厂商及台湾代工企业负责人的长期直接合作，英伟达得以锁定优先配额并获得低于同业约两成的采购报价。当职业经理人接管经营大权后，公司治理重心自然向风险控制、现金流安全与股票回购倾斜。此前克雷斯在内部决策中便曾对超大规模客户的高风险担保方案持审慎态度，未来英伟达对海外新兴算力云厂商的信用兜底标准势必趋严，那些高度依赖亚洲跨境客户现金流的中小算力运营商将首先面临融资收缩压力。 1.3 华盛顿商业温和派丧失核心政策支点 在企业经营调整之外，黄仁勋的退出打破了华盛顿围绕对华芯片政策形成的内部制衡。过去四年间，美国政策界在对华算力问题上始终存在两种思路：国会两党安全强硬派主张对先进算力实施严格物理隔离，防止任何前沿芯片或算力服务流向中国；而以黄仁勋为代表的产业界力量则反复向行政部门陈述，适度保留合规减配芯片出口与海外云算力服务，能够使中国人工智能研发体系持续停留在美系软硬件架构内，从而降低中国企业全力投入本土替代芯片的商业动力。 在特朗普政府第二任期的前半段，这一商业逻辑在白宫与商务部内部获得了相当程度的采纳。以商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克（Howard Lutnick）为代表的官员倾向于将芯片许可纳入双边经贸谈判框架，美国政府不仅在 2025 年撤销了前任政府制定的全球人工智能扩散分级限制，还在 2026 年允许英伟达在缴纳 25% 收入分成的前提下逐案申请对华出售部分高性能芯片，同时搁置了多项针对东南亚数据中心的额外许可证规则与实体清单增列建议。然而，随着黄仁勋因涉华合规风波辞职，英伟达在华盛顿的政策游说信誉严重受损，财政部与国会强硬派随即公开批评商务部在出口执法上过于宽松。微软、亚马逊等本就支持限制竞争对手海外芯片销售的美国本土超大规模云厂商，则在政策讨论中占据了更有利的位置。产业界反对全面禁令的最强声音消失后，行政部门内部主张保留政策弹性的温和派已难以阻挡管制全面收紧。 第二章  中期选举后美国出口管制的立法转向 2.1 两院控制权易手打通积压法案排期 英伟达管理层震荡恰逢 2026 年 11 月美国中期选举落幕，政治周期的叠加进一步放大了政策转向的确定性。截至 11 月中旬的计票结果显示，民主党在众议院赢得逾 250 个席位，并在参议院取得至少 54 个席位，将于 2027 年 1 月第 120 届国会开幕时全面接管参众两院的立法议程与各关键委员会主席职位。在美国对华科技管制议题上，两党基本立场高度一致，此前多项芯片与云算力限制法案之所以迟迟未能走完立法程序，症结主要在于国会内部的议程排期与跨议题政治博弈，而非对管制本身存在分歧。 回顾 2026 年年中，参议院在起草《2027 财年国防授权法案》（NDAA）修正案时，曾计划将四项涉华芯片与云算力管制法案一并打包纳入；但由于民主党议员当时不满白宫未经国会授权采取的中东军事行动及国防开支增幅，在 7 月份的程序性表决中投下反对票，使法案仅获 50 票支持而未能达到终结辩论所需的 60 票门槛。中期选举结果揭晓与英伟达事件发酵后，立法推进出现了两个明确的时间窗口。第一个窗口是 2026 年 11 月至 12 月的国会“跛脚鸭会期”，参众两院军事委员会与外交事务委员会负责人正围绕国防授权法案展开最终协调，力争在年底休会前将各方共识度较高的芯片管制条款保留在最终版本中。第二个窗口则是 2027 年 1 月新国会就位之后，届时查克·舒默（Chuck Schumer）预计重返参议院多数党领袖职位，而长期推动严管芯片出口的伊丽莎白·沃伦（Elizabeth Warren）有望出任拥有出口管制管辖权的参议院银行委员会主席，即使部分条款未能在年底挂靠国防法案通过，明年也将获得优先排期并快速推进单独立法。 2.2 管制主导权由行政裁量移交国会立法 下一阶段美国对华算力管控最显著的制度特征，是规则制定权从行政部门的部门规章向国会成文法转移。在既有体制下，美国出口管制的具体技术参数与许可证政策主要由商务部工业与安全局通过修订《出口管理条例》来执行。这种行政主导模式赋予了总统和商务部长较大的自由裁量空间，使其能够根据宏观经贸关系的变化灵活调节审批尺度。例如在 2026 年下半年中美围绕经贸协议延期、关键矿产及农产品采购展开的贸易磋商中，放宽或收紧特定芯片出口许可一直是美方谈判团队手中的可调工具。 国会正在推进的一系列法案，核心意图正是压缩行政部门在国家安全技术领域的自由裁量空间。其中最具代表性的《AI 监督法案》（AI OVERWATCH Act）明确提出，将面向受关注国家出口先进人工智能芯片的审批流程纳入类似对外武器销售的国会监督框架，不仅要求撤销现有相关出口许可证，还规定商务部在发放特定许可前必须提交国会审查，且在两年内不得随意下调受控芯片的技术门槛。面对国会控制权即将更迭以及英伟达事件引发的舆论压力，白宫近期已改变此前对限制自身裁量权法案的消极态度，转而向国会委员会提供具体技术修订意见。对白宫而言，主动参与立法协调既能避免法案条款过度侵蚀外交权限，又能将国会强硬立法转化为双边经贸谈判中的外部约束借口。一旦核心算力限制由行政规章升格为国会法律，未来即便双边经贸关系出现阶段性缓和，美方行政当局也难以单方面松动算力出口限制。 第三章  下一阶段对华算力管控的四项机制演进 3.1 远程访问法案将云端算力纳入出口许可 在具体管制工具上，对现有跨境算力商业模式影响最深远的是《远程访问安全法案》（RASA，H.R. 2683）。该法案已于 2026 年 1 月在众议院以 369 票赞成、22 票反对通过，目前正待参议院银行委员会推进或并入国防法案。过去近二十年间，美国出口管制遵循传统的物理跨境原则：只要搭载高端加速卡的服务器实际部署在新加坡、马来西亚、中东或欧洲的数据中心内，未发生硬件实体的物理转移，中国企业通过网络远程租用这些服务器训练模型，在现行法规下并不属于需要申请许可证的“出口”行为。 从经济利益与安全监控的角度看，这种类似“离岸美元市场”的运行方式原本对美方颇为有利：算力租金收入归属美系芯片商与海外云运营商，服务器物理控制权留在境外从而具备随时断网的条件，同时还能在一定程度上掌握客户的算力调用规模。但 Megaspeed 等案例曝光后，美国国会普遍认为离岸云租赁已成为规避实体芯片禁令的主要通道。RASA 法案通过修订《出口管制改革法》，正式授权商务部工业与安全局对受控物项的云端远程访问实施许可管理，并要求云算力服务商建立类似金融机构反洗钱合规的客户身份穿透核查制度。这意味着监管边界从传统的海关实体货物查验，延伸至全球数据中心的网络账户与算力分配层面。法案一旦生效，遍布亚太、中东及欧美的新兴算力云厂商若继续向未经许可的中国实体提供前沿芯片远程算力，将直接面临二级制裁与断供处罚。 在国会推进立法的同时，行政部门已于 2026 年 11 月 16 日先行发布《应对先进半导体远程访问》暂行最终规则，新增《出口管理条例》第 744.24 条与第 742.6 条，并正式废止旧《人工智能扩散框架》。新规规定，全球任何数据中心（含共享底层资源的联网数据中心）若向总部或最终母公司位于中国大陆及澳门的企业（含经由第三国子公司或第三方中介代训）提供超过 1,200 万综合总处理性能（aggregate TPP）的先进算力访问，须事先取得逐案许可；存量达标服务须在规则生效后 90 天内正式取得许可，仅纯粹的商业推荐系统可获特定排除（不含任何生成式模型）。此外，新规对印尼、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和巴西五国增设先进计算物项出口许可（美资母公司可凭按月报告豁免地域许可，但对华分配算力仍受用途审查），并收紧了前端晶圆厂与封测企业推翻未获批设计商芯片分类推定的路径。 3.2 芯片安全法案推行硬件位置强制核验 针对通过第三国中间商拆解、转运实体服务器的灰色贸易链条，美国国会同步推出了《芯片安全法案》（Chip Security Act，S. 1705 / H.R. 3447），该法案已在众议院外交事务委员会以 42 比 0 全票获批。过去几年，尽管美国执法部门多次查处违规转运案件——例如 2026 年 3 月美国司法部曾就一起涉及约 25 亿美元英伟达芯片服务器的违规转运案提起公诉——但依靠人工追踪全球多级分销网络的执法成本极高，难以从根本上阻断硬件流转。 《芯片安全法案》的解决思路是将执法监督职能前置到芯片硬件架构之中，强制要求所有出口的先进人工智能芯片和服务器集成防篡改的位置验证技术，并规定许可证持有人一旦发现芯片偏离批准地点或出现人为拆改迹象，必须立即向商务部报告。在工程原理上，这类位置核验主要依托芯片内置的硬件安全密钥与网络通信时延测算：运行中的加速卡需定期与指定验证节点进行加密通信，根据光信号在光纤中的物理传输时延确定服务器所处的地理范围。英伟达此前其实已经推出名为“集群智能”（Fleet Intelligence）的数据中心管理遥测工具，具备监测集群运行指标与物理位置的能力，但此前仅面向申请官方认证的云合作伙伴自愿开放。新立法相当于把这一自愿商业工具转变为法定出厂条件，使合规核查贯穿芯片从出厂点亮到日常运行的全生命周期，大幅提高了通过物理走私获取大规模可用集群的技术门槛。 3.3 多边设备协同法案收紧上游产线扩张 除堵住海外云租赁与实体芯片转运外，《AI 监督法案》（AI OVERWATCH Act）和《硬件技术管制多边协调法案》（MATCH Act，S. 4281）分别从成品芯片配额与上游制造设备两端收紧了约束。《AI 监督法案》要求先进算力芯片优先保障美国国内市场需求，废除面向受关注国家的存量许可，并通过严格的国会审查阻止芯片企业专门针对管制红线设计减配特供产品。 《硬件技术管制多边协调法案》则将重点放在半导体制造设备的多边规则统一上。过去一段时间，由于美国单边管制严于盟友标准，荷兰与日本的设备制造商仍可向中国非受限晶圆厂出售部分深紫外浸润式光刻机（DUV）及刻蚀、沉积设备，并提供现场维护与备件支持，这为中国本土扩大先进逻辑芯片与高带宽内存产能留出了窗口。MATCH 法案要求行政部门推动荷、日等盟友将半导体制造设备的出口限制全面向美方标准看齐，填补设备品类与售后维修服务上的管制差异。荷兰政府已围绕该议题与美方进行了多轮沟通，力求在配合多边安全协调的同时减少美国域外管辖对本国设备企业正常运营的冲击。四项法案相互配合，构成了覆盖制造设备、实体芯片、云端访问与行政审批的完整制度框架。 第四章  算力管制升级对中国人工智能产业的影响 4.1 离岸算力收缩改变大模型训练成本结构 随着英伟达内部合规整顿与美国国会立法进程提速，中国人工智能企业首先面临的是海外算力租赁渠道的实质性收窄。在正式立法落地之前，英伟达为降低自身监管风险，近几个月已主动削减了超过半数的亚洲预批准买家名单，并指导全球云合作伙伴将非中国客户的服务占比提升至 51% 以上，同时要求部分云厂商配合核验最终算力使用方身份。在黄仁勋离任后，东南亚、中东及欧美的新兴算力云运营商出于维护硬件供应与债务融资安全的考虑，势必加快清理涉华高风险业务。过去部分国内研发机构借助海外分布式机房获取最新一代加速卡集群的做法，将面临更高的合规审查门槛与断供不确定性。尤其是 11 月 16 日 BIS 远程算力新规出台后，设备已运抵机房、合同已签署及租金已预付均不再确保服务持续履行，存量服务须在 90 天内取得许可，租用美资海外机房或与推荐业务共用算力亦须重审许可条件。训练高度依赖单一境外集群的国内企业，近期不得不优先落实未使用费用退还、训练数据与模型检查点导出及迁移安排。 硬件获取渠道的收紧，直接改变了国内大模型研发的成本函数与技术选型偏好。当单纯依靠扩充最新制程芯片数量来推高模型规模变得不再经济甚至不可行时，工程优化的重心自然转向提高单位算力的词元产出效率。在模型架构层面，混合专家模型（MoE）中单次激活参数比例的控制、长上下文场景下键值缓存（KV Cache）的压缩以及稀疏注意力机制的改进，成为对冲硬件显存带宽约束的主要手段；在商业落地层面，企业不再盲目追求全能型超大参数基座的重复训练，而是更加注重中等规模模型在垂直行业场景中的推理性价比。算力约束在增加前沿探索难度的同时，也促使行业资金与算力资源更快向具备底层系统工程能力的研发团队集中。 4.2 外部渠道收紧加速本土算力商业化验证 从产业演进的激励机制看，美方全面封堵离岸算力租赁与减配芯片供应，在客观上产生了另一重深远影响：它消除了中国人工智能企业对外部算力渠道的观望心理，加快了国产算力芯片与本土软件栈的商业化磨合。在半导体行业中，一款加速卡能否从“可用”走向“好用”，取决于是否有足够多的一线算法团队在真实的大规模训练和高并发推理任务中持续使用它，并在实践中不断完善编译器、通信库与底层算子。过去几年，只要企业仍能通过合规减配硬件或海外机房租用到英伟达算力，出于节省代码迁移与调试时间的短期商业考量，多数团队仍倾向于优先使用成熟的 CUDA 环境，导致国产芯片较难进入最核心的前沿模型预训练环节。 随着外部替代通道逐步关闭，迁移至本土算力架构的长期确定性收益开始超过短期工程改造成本，国内头部模型厂商与国产芯片企业的协同深度明显提升。2026 年以来，这一转向已在多个标杆模型上得到验证：2 月，智谱发布的旗舰模型 GLM-5 完全基于十万卡规模的华为昇腾 910B 集群与昇思框架完成训练，并实现了对多款国产加速卡的推理支持；4 月至 8 月间，DeepSeek 推出 1.6 万亿总参数的混合专家模型 V4，同步开源了针对昇腾处理器深度优化的推理算子与社区插件；6 月，美团发布的 LongCat 2.0 模型同样依托国产算力集群从头完成了预训练流程。当头部商业应用与基础模型持续在国产硬件上运行，软件生态短板便能在高频工程反馈中逐步补齐，原本流向海外算力租赁市场的资金也将回流支撑本土晶圆制造、先进封装与集群互联技术的迭代。 4.3 硬件底座分化削弱跨国开源软件协同 算力管制升级带来的另一项结构性外溢效应，是中美工程界在人工智能开源软件领域的共生关系面临拆解。过去两年间，全球开源大模型生态呈现出一个值得关注的现象：受限于硬件性能与数量的中国研究团队，为充分挖掘现有英伟达芯片的计算效率，开发并开源了一批高质量的底层通信与矩阵运算库，包括面向混合专家架构的 DeepEP、DeepGEMM 以及月之暗面发布的注意力优化内核 FlashKDA。这些底层软件创新被广泛整合进 vLLM、SGLang 等国际主流开源推理框架中，显著降低了全球中小科技企业与初创公司部署大模型的算力成本。 对于英伟达而言，繁荣的开源模型生态原本是维持其市场地位的重要支撑。由于谷歌、亚马逊、微软等北美超大规模云服务商均在大规模部署自研专用芯片，闭源模型巨头对通用图形处理器的长期议价能力不断增强；只有开源模型保持强劲竞争力，全球各地的企业私有化部署与区域云服务商才会持续采购英伟达硬件。黄仁勋在任期间积极支持开源社区，英伟达工程师团队也与中国开源实验室保持了密切的技术磨合。在黄仁勋离职以及远程访问限制推进后，由职业经理人管理的英伟达出于合规审慎与短期财务回报考量，预计将缩减涉华开源技术协作；与此同时，随着中国研发团队将优化重心转向国产异构芯片架构，其编写的底层算子与编译工具将不再直接适配美系硬件，部分关键性能优化甚至可能转为内部专有技术。跨国开源技术流动的放缓，将在客观上增加西方初创企业获取低成本开源推理方案的难度。 第五章  全球算力基础设施的长期演进趋势 5.1 单一硬件架构主导地位逐步松动 从全球科技产业演化的长周期审视，黄仁勋卸任英伟达首席执行官，标志着由单一企业、单一创始人及单一软硬件生态主导全球算力扩张的阶段告一段落。过去十余年，全球人工智能计算建立在高度一体化的跨国分工之上：依托台湾地区的先进晶圆代工、韩国的高带宽存储芯片、英伟达的并行计算架构与 CUDA 软件体系，再结合中美两国庞大的工程人才储备，全行业得以沿着统一的技术标准快速迭代。黄仁勋凭借创始人的战略魄力与商业手腕，在复杂的地缘政治环境中尽力维持了这一跨国商业网络的运转；他的离开表明，企业层面的商业斡旋已无法继续对冲大国安全竞争带来的制度性分割。 在接下来的产业周期中，全球算力市场将同时经历横向竞争扩散与纵向区域分化。在西方市场内部，步入职业经理人治理阶段的英伟达将更加注重资本开支纪律与股东回报，过去依靠创始人个人承诺大规模锁死上游存储与代工产能的做法将有所收敛，预计到 2028 年前后将有更大比例的先进制造与存储产能流向云巨头自研专用芯片及博通、AMD 等竞争厂商。在跨国格局层面，若美国国会通过成文法封堵远程云访问并强制植入芯片位置核验，过去连接东西方算力供需的灰色中间地带将消退，全球算力基础设施将更可能演变为美系生态与本土自主生态各自独立演进的二元结构。 5.2 系统工程能力成为算力竞争核心尺度 出口管制立法的全面升级固然会在未来数年内给中国获取尖端半导体设备与算力硬件制造持续障碍，但算力基础设施的长期竞争力并非仅由单颗芯片的制程节点唯一决定。随着人工智能应用逐步由早期的大规模预训练拓展至高频复杂推理与产业级部署，衡量算力体系效能的标尺正在从单卡峰值浮点算力，转向涵盖集群高速互联、电力能源供给、算法架构效率与行业场景落地的综合系统能力。 在单颗芯片制程受到外部设备限制的条件下，系统级工程创新提供了明确的突围路径。通过高带宽光互联与超节点技术将大规模国产加速卡组网协同，利用中国在发电装机容量、电网调配与数据中心基础设施建设上的成本优势分摊集群能耗，并结合算法层面对计算与通信冗余的持续压缩，完全能够在集群整体吞吐与单次词元推理成本上弥补单卡物理性能的差距。黄仁勋辞职事件所触发的美国对华算力管控升级，在关闭外部便利算力通道的同时，也促使中国人工智能产业将资源更集中地投向底层硬件制造、系统软件编译与高价值行业应用。在两套技术体系平行演进的新阶段，真正决定长期产业格局的，将是哪一方能够以更可持续的能源与资本投入，将算力稳定转化为实体经济的生产率增益。 articles.title: 交易商开始把美国铜运往中国，贸易流向逆转
articles.summary: 关税预期降温与中国市场极度紧缺，正驱动全球铜贸易流向发生根本性转变。交易商已开始将积压在美国港口的铜运往中国，终结了过去两年间铜持续涌入美国的单向格局。 据英国《金融时报》报道，约六艘运铜船已离开长滩和洛杉矶港口驶向中国。彭博稍早于11月19日援引知情人士称，已有订舱完成，部分原定运往美国的铜也被改道中国，目前涉及规模约为数万吨。这一流向逆转标志着持续近两年的"抢运入美"交易开始瓦解。 铜价本周在伦敦金属交易所大幅下挫，从上月底逾14,670美元的高位跌至不足12,600美元。高盛在致投资者报告中指出，市场本周已开始计价美国可能不对铜征税——但这仅是市场预期的转变，美国并未正式宣布放弃铜关税。 94%库存积压美国，套利窗口转向中国 过去两年，对特朗普政府征收铜关税的预期驱使交易商将大量铜运入美国 。据大宗商品机构Marex数据，目前约94%的伦敦金属交易所与芝加哥商品交易所仓库铜库存位于美国境内，而两年前这一比例仅为20%。彭博援引交易商估算，美国铜库存总量约达200万吨。 然而， 随着关税预期降温，美国的价格优势已不复存在。 Marex高级金属策略师Alastair Munro表示，芝加哥商品交易所相对伦铜的升水已消失，并转为伦铜升水。与此同时，中国市场的极度紧缺令当地溢价飙升，洋山铜进口溢价在过去一周内翻倍，升至约每吨500美元的历史纪录。 研究机构Benchmark分析师Albert Mackenzie表示，"中国方面出现了有利的套利空间，源于当地市场的紧张状态和高额溢价。越来越多的人，尤其是在中国的交易商，认为关税可能已经'死了'。" 长滩率先出货，新奥尔良和巴尔的摩库存亦被提走 从出货地点来看，地理位置最靠近亚洲的加利福尼亚州长滩库存率先启动出运。据《金融时报》，交易商随后也开始从新奥尔良和巴尔的摩提货——后两地存放着规模更大的库存，但需以美国市价买入，方能实现更大的中美价差套利。 据彭博，从美国西海岸运往中国约需两周，而从新奥尔良出发，加上仓库出库时间，整个流程约需六周至两个月。这意味着中国市场的紧张局面短期内难以缓解，但也令交易商面临铜到港时套利窗口已关闭的风险。 一位不愿具名的交易商表示，"10个月来，所有人都在拼命往美国运铜，因为大家以为美国要对铜征关税。现在中国库存已低至以小时而非周来计算使用量的程度。"该交易商预计，"不难设想明年春节前（2月）有数十万吨铜抵达中国"——这是对未来走势的判断，而非已成事实。 关税政策悬而未决，市场自行定价 美国政府在关税问题上的沉默是此轮预期转变的重要背景。据彭博，商务部原定于年中向特朗普提交精炼铜关税报告，但此后政府对此保持沉默。 Kpler数据显示，本月预计运入美国的铜量不足10月创纪录水平的一半，显示铜流入美国的势头已明显放缓。分析师同时指出，当前的出货量也反映出交易商的担忧——若关税于明年初突然落地，正在运输途中的铜将面临损失。 BMO Capital Markets商品分析师Helen Amos表示，"如果我们开始看到交易商采取行动，准备将阴极铜从美国运往中国，我会对此不引发政府某种回应感到意外。"这意味着，这场流向逆转本身或将重新将铜关税议题推回政治议程。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
